query: For a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain the accelerated coupled degradation and why it occurs? Specify a controlled comparison capable of distinguishing the proposed explanation, predict the changes in total degradation and the individual wear and corrosion responses relative to a matched baseline, define the relevant boundary conditions, identify supporting evidence, and give a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Under simultaneous mechanical wear and hot Na2SO4-K2SO4 corrosion (700 °C), the interdendritic Laves-rich phase in a eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) acts as a local anode while the fcc matrix acts as a cathode; repeated removal of the initially formed oxide scale by sliding exposes fresh, electrochemically coupled interfaces so that galvanic-accelerated dissolution of the Laves phase creates trenches that act as crack initiators and wear debris sources. The dynamic micro-galvanic coupling therefore produces total material loss that exceeds the arithmetic sum of purely corrosive mass loss and purely mechanical wear.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast dual-phase fcc γ + C14 Laves eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g. AlCoCrFeNi2.1) with {γ/Laves} lamellae ~0.5 µm, hardness ≈ 6 GPa, no prior oxidation.
generation.intervention: Simultaneous pin-on-disc sliding at 5 N normal load, 0.1 m s⁻¹, in a flowing 0.3 Pa O2 + molten 75 wt % Na2SO4 / 25 wt % K2SO4 salt film at 700 °C for 2 h.
generation.conditions: Temperature 650 – 750 °C; contact stress 80 – 150 MPa; sliding speed ≤ 0.2 m s⁻¹; salt film thickness 2–5 µm; environment contains ≤ 0.3 Pa O2 and no Cl-; surfaces initially oxide-free.
generation.structural_mediator: Lamellar γ/Laves interfaces forming micron-scale galvanic couples that emerge at the wear track after each oxide removal event.
generation.mechanism:
1) Sliding removes nascent Cr-, Al-rich oxides, cyclically exposing fresh γ/Laves interfaces.
2) In molten sulfate, the high-Cr/Si Mo-rich Laves phase becomes anodic to the fcc γ matrix, dissolving preferentially (ΔE ≈ 150 mV).
3) Selective dissolution undermines adjacent γ lamellae, creating undercut trenches that spall as wear debris, raising mechanical wear rate.
4) Newly exposed area enlarges electrochemical current, so corrosion rate rises; debris also traps salt, sustaining local chemistry.
5) The positive feedback causes total material loss to exceed the linear addition of separate wear and corrosion losses.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to a matched test in which galvanic coupling is suppressed (homogenised single-phase alloy or electrically insulated phases), the coupled γ/Laves alloy will show: (a) ≥ 2× higher total mass loss; (b) ≈ 1.5× higher sliding wear rate; (c) ≈ 1.5× higher time-integrated corrosion current density; the synergistic term (Δm_coupled − Δm_wear-only − Δm_corrosion-only) will be positive.
generation.baseline: Same alloy tested at 700 °C in (i) wear-only (dry argon), (ii) corrosion-only (static molten sulfate, no sliding), and (iii) coupled but after solutionizing at 1250 °C/2 h to produce a single-phase γ solid solution (micro-galvanic network removed).
generation.boundary: Effect expected only while (i) multiphase microstructure with electrical contact is preserved, (ii) oxide scale removal rate ≥ oxide growth rate, and (iii) molten salt prevents rapid formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale. Below 550 °C or without molten salt, galvanic dissolution is transport-limited and synergy collapses.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of potential difference between γ and Laves phases at 700 °C in molten sulfate is not yet measured; predicted acceleration factors (1.5–2×) are estimates with ±50 % uncertainty.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two pin specimens: (A) as-cast γ/Laves eutectic; (B) identical alloy solutionized to single-phase γ. Perform identical coupled wear-corrosion tests (parameters above). Measure (i) mass change, (ii) open-circuit and tribo-current during sliding, (iii) coefficient of friction, (iv) post-test cross-sectional SEM/EDS for selective dissolution.
measurements: Area fraction of dissolved Laves at wear track
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If specimen A does not show a statistically significant (>20 %) increase in both wear rate and corrosion charge relative to specimen B, or if total mass loss for A ≤ (wear-only + corrosion-only) baseline within experimental error, the micro-galvanic acceleration hypothesis is falsified.
